text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default. This guarantees keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation in one click, solving the most common keyboard accessibility failure. The trade-off is screen space, but it’s negligible compared to the usability gain—especially on mobile where touch targets are already crowded.

name: Reader
text: Large skip links push primary content below the fold on short pages, hurting users who rely on context. A hidden skip link with keyboard-only focus solves the space issue without the risk. Test both with real keyboard users—success is when they reach the main content faster without confusion.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **hidden skip link** that only appears when focused via keyboard. This keeps screen space intact for all users while giving keyboard navigators a clear, immediate path to main content. The trade-off is a small extra step for sighted keyboard users to discover the link—but it prevents the far worse failure of trapping them in endless navigation. Real-world testing shows this pattern works; failing it means excluding people who rely on keyboards.

name: Reader
text: Hidden skip links still confuse first-time keyboard users who don’t know the link exists until they tab—real risk of wasted keystrokes. A better alternative: a small, always-visible skip link with reduced motion and high contrast, placed just above primary navigation. Settle it with Playwright MCP automated keyboard tests measuring time-to-main-content for both patterns—real users confirm which one works faster without guesswork.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a compact, high-contrast skip link always visible above primary nav—tested with Playwright MCP for keyboard nav success by accessibility-w1.
